Definition: from G2513; to cleanse (literally or figuratively):--(make) clean(-se), purge, purify.
BiblicalUsage: To cleanse is what Jesus did when He touched the leper and said I will, be thou clean, and the leprosy departed, and the ten lepers were cleansed as they went, and John says if we confess our sins He is faithful and just to forgive us and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. The word holds the touch on the skin and the washing of the soul together, and the same Lord does both.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the leper's prayer is mine too, Lord, if Thou wilt, Thou canst make me clean. I hold that confession is the way the cleansing comes, because He is faithful and just to do what He promised.
